analysis.evidence: The victors seize both כָּל רְכֻשׁ סְדֹם וַעֲמֹרָה, all the property of Sodom and Gomorrah, and כָּל אָכְלָם, all their food. The closing וַיֵּלֵכוּ, “and they left,” completes the account of the plunder.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ is prefixed to a Qal wayyiqtol verb in the third person masculine plural.

analysis.evidence: אֶת introduces כָּל רְכֻשׁ סְדֹם וַעֲמֹרָה, “all the possessions of Sodom and Gomorrah,” as the first definite object of וַיִּקְחוּ, “they took.” The parallel וְאֶת כָּל אָכְלָם marks the second object, “all their food.”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל רְכֻשׁ סְדֹם וַעֲמֹרָה, רְכֻשׁ denotes the possessions of Sodom and Gomorrah collectively. כָּל indicates that the victors took all of those possessions.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun governing רְכֻשׁ, with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add the root רכש and its noun רְכוּשׁ for acquired possessions. The source’s personal-name gloss does not fit this occurrence.
draft.definition: Property or goods that someone owns, taken collectively.
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:5 pairs רְכוּשָׁם, “their possessions,” with רָכָשׁוּ, “they had acquired.”

analysis.evidence: The raiders took כָּל רְכֻשׁ סְדֹם וַעֲמֹרָה, “all the possessions of Sodom and Gomorrah,” along with כָּל אָכְלָם, “all their food.” Both phrases describe what the raiders carried away.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with no prefix or suffix. The following names סְדֹם וַעֲמֹרָה identify whose possessions they were.

draft.change: Add a standalone place-name article for סְדֹם, keyed by its own consonants סדמ. The supplied root סגר does not account for this form.
draft.definition: סְדֹם is the Hebrew name of the city of Sodom.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:19 names Sodom alongside Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim in its description of Canaanite territory.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל רְכֻשׁ סְדֹם וַעֲמֹרָה, “all the possessions of Sodom and Gomorrah,” סְדֹם and עֲמֹרָה name the two cities whose possessions were taken.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל אָכְלָם, “all their food,” כָּל refers to the entire food supply taken from Sodom and Gomorrah. The phrase parallels כָּל רְכֻשׁ, “all the property.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state before אָכְלָם.

analysis.evidence: The raiders took all the possessions of Sodom and Gomorrah and then וְאֶת כָּל אָכְלָם, “and all their provisions.” The parallel objects identify the food supply as part of what the raiders seized.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state with a third-person masculine plural possessive suffix.
